title: Nessa and the Lost Dragonet
markdown:
Candlecrag was a wild place, even for a witch’s abode. The frosty wind around the snowy shelves was a different sort of chill. Yet inside Nessa’s cottage the hearth crackled with a glorious warmth, casting shadows that danced like ancient spirits on the walls. Young Nessa, a witch whose midnight hair framed eyes of polished amber, hummed a little witchy tune. She polished her spectacles with a cloth as soft as a cloud. Those spectacles were vital for spotting the tiniest most magical ingredients. Her Grandmother, a witch of immense wisdom and even greater patience, had set her a quest: to find a bloom of celestial grace, the Moonpetal, from the shadowed fringes of the Whispering Woods. A promise Nessa had made, to complete this task before the sun dipped below the horizon. And to Nessa, a promise was a treasure to be guarded.

“A promise is a promise, Grandmother,” Nessa had declared, voice as clear and bright as a freshly kindled flame. She imagined the delicate silver-white petals unfurling under the moon’s gentle gaze.

From his throne of comfort beside the hearth, nestled on a plump well-worn cushion, Cassian, Nessa’s most esteemed goat, offered a sage Maa. Cassian was no ordinary goat. His ears twitched like the most sensitive antennae, catching the faintest whisper. His nose, perpetually curious, seemed to sniff out secrets from leagues away. He wasn’t merely a pet. He was a bona fide eavesdropper, and he’d caught every word of Nessa’s important promise.

“Maa-aa! Venturing out? Into the woods? All by your solitary self?” A low rumbling bleat that vibrated with importance. Whiskers quivered, eager. “That, my dear Nessa, sounds like a task demanding two. Or rather, one wise witch and one exceptionally clever goat. Especially if there are intriguing scents to investigate.”

Nessa sighed, a soft puff that momentarily misted her spectacles. “It’s but a small quest, dear Cassian, for a Moonpetal. Grandmother needs it for her special slumber tonic.” She attempted a firm tone, but Cassian’s persistent gaze was as hard to deflect as a charging boar.

“A small quest can blossom into a grand expedition if one is not adequately prepared! And who is better suited for preparation than your steadfast companion? I possess superior hoof-grip for those icy patches, you know.” He nudged a stray broom with his nose, then gave a mischievous flick of his beard. He rather relished the prospect of an adventure, particularly one where his unsolicited, yet invariably brilliant, advice could be dispensed. And, of course, the potential discovery of an exceptionally succulent patch of moss.

And so, with Cassian trotting with unwavering determination beside her, hooves crunching on the crisp fallen snow with a satisfying rhythm, Nessa set off toward the Whispering Woods. The trees, cloaked in a thick silent mantle of white, stood like ancient stoic sentinels, branches reaching toward a pale wintry sky. A world of profound hushed beauty. Nessa breathed deeply, the clean cold air filling her lungs. She reveled in the quiet majesty of the snow-laden pines, the soft hush that seemed to embrace the world in a gentle comforting blanket.

“It’s all rather… white, wouldn’t you agree?” Cassian sniffed the air with an exaggerated flourish. “A remarkable scarcity of intriguing scents, if I’m to be frank. Mostly just… cold. And a faint whisper of pine. Terribly predictable.” A small snort. “Though I suppose the snow does lend itself to excellent bouncing, if one is so inclined.”

Suddenly a tiny desperate squeak pierced the stillness, like a fragile bell rung in profound sorrow. So small, so fraught with woe, that it made Nessa’s heart clench. Both she and Cassian halted abruptly.

“What was that sound?” Nessa whispered. Her witch’s instincts tingling, a prickle of awareness. Amber eyes scanned the snowy landscape.

Following the faint piteous sound, they discovered, huddled beneath the broad sheltering bough of an ancient oak, a creature no larger than Nessa’s winter mitten. A dragonet, no bigger than a teacup, scales shimmering like emeralds even in the dim wintry light. Tiny iridescent wings drooped sadly. Little snout buried in delicate paws. Utterly, completely lost. A miniature statue of sorrow amidst the vast expanse of white.

“Oh, you poor lost thing!” Nessa’s heart softened instantly, melting faster than snow under a warm gaze. She knelt carefully, extending a hand as if offering a sanctuary. “Are you quite alright?”

The dragonet peeked up, eyes wide and blue like chips of the winter sky. Another plaintive squeak, echoing the emptiness of the woods.

“He has lost his way,” Cassian stated with great certainty, ears now fully attuned. “Likely wandered off in pursuit of a particularly glittering icicle. They have a predilection for such things, you know. Dragons. A peculiar fondness for anything that sparkles, even if it’s merely frozen water.” He nudged a stray snowflake with his hoof.

Nessa gently scooped up the dragonet. Surprisingly warm against her palm, a tiny beacon of life in the chilly woods. “My Grandmother requires a Moonpetal. But I cannot leave you here all alone. My promise to her suddenly feels… a little less significant than this little dragonet’s safety.” The Moonpetal, though precious, was but a flower. This tiny creature was a life.

Cassian nudged her hand with his soft muzzle. “Maa! Of course! The Moonpetal can await. Assisting a friend in distress—that’s a promise worth honoring too. Besides,” a sly wink, “who knows what marvels we might uncover when we’re not on the hunt for mere flowers? What is your name, little spark?”

The dragonet, startled by the sudden warmth and kindness, gave a tiny puff of smoke smelling faintly of cinnamon and pine needles, and chirped, “Spark!”

“Well, Spark.” A determined glint in Nessa’s eye that rivaled the sparkle of the snow. “We shall assist you in finding your way home.”

Their quest had taken an unexpected, yet profoundly wonderful, turn. The Whispering Woods, which had seemed so quiet and serene, now pulsed with purpose. They ventured deeper, Nessa carefully cradling Spark in her cupped hands, Cassian leading the way, keen nose sniffing the frosty air, ears swiveling like twin radar dishes.

Their path led them to a small gurgling stream, frozen over in places but still with water rushing beneath the icy surface. The ice looked deceptively smooth and inviting. Nessa knew from her grandmother’s tales that ice could be treacherous.

“Pro tip from someone who learned the hard way,” Cassian declared, surveying the ice with a critical eye. “Never trust a smiling ice patch. Always test it. With a hoof. A strong reliable hoof, like mine.” He nudged a loose pebble-sized stone toward the ice. It slid across without a crack.

Nessa, holding Spark carefully, looked around. “Perhaps we can construct a tiny bridge?” She spotted fallen branches near the bank, sturdy and long. With a bit of whispered magic she coaxed them to snap and arrange themselves, weaving and binding into a sturdy, albeit slightly wobbly, bridge. Cassian, with a confident Maa that sounded like a trumpet call, trotted across first, testing its strength with each sure-footed step. It held firm.

Once safely across, a sound drifted from further within the woods: a distant echoing roar. Not fierce. Filled with longing and worry. Spark perked up instantly, tiny wings fluttering. “Mama!” Stronger now, filled with recognition.

Following the sound, they found themselves in a small secluded clearing. And there, pacing anxiously, was a magnificent larger dragon. Scales the colour of a fiery sunset, shifting and shimmering. She looked up as they approached. Great golden eyes widened with overwhelming relief.

“Spark!” Like rumbling thunder, yet soft with maternal love. She swooped down, great wings beating gently, nudging her little one with her snout. “Oh, my brave little Spark! Where have you been? I was so worried!”

Spark, chirping excitedly, nuzzled his mother’s warm scales. Then he turned his bright blue eyes toward Nessa and Cassian, giving them a tiny grateful puff of cinnamon smoke.

The mother dragon lowered her great head. “You have brought my Spark back to me. I am forever in your debt, little witch, and… goat.” She winked at Cassian, who puffed out his chest proudly. He’d always suspected he was destined for greatness.

Nessa felt a warmth spread through her, far cozier than any hearth fire. “We’re just glad he’s safe. It was an unexpected promise, but a very important one.”

As the mother dragon and Spark ascended, joyous roars echoing, trails of shimmering heat in the cold air, Nessa and Cassian watched them go. The Moonpetal was forgotten for now. Walking back toward their warm cottage, the snow felt softer, the air lighter. Cassian, for once, was quiet, ears still twitching but nose less busy.

“You know, Nessa,” he finally bleated, nudging her gently, voice unusually thoughtful, “sometimes the best promises are the ones you didn’t even know you were making.”

Nessa smiled, genuine, reaching her amber eyes. “I agree, Cassian.” Hand-in-hoof they stepped back into the cozy glow of their little home. Grandmother’s tonic, Nessa suspected, could wait one more moon. Spark, somewhere above the peaks, was already home.
characters: Nessa (young witch of Candlecrag), Cassian (eavesdropping goat of excellent advice)
